data.reasoning: Only one valid report (deepseek) was produced; the others failed due to API/parse errors. The valid report correctly identified the package as safe, recognizing that the download domain (codeiumdata.com) is owned by the upstream vendor (Codeium) and that the pinned checksums mitigate supply-chain risks. No malicious injections were found in the PKGBUILD or auxiliary scripts.
data.disagreement_analysis: The apparent disagreement was caused by tool failures (API errors and parse errors) in the other models, rather than genuine security disagreements. The deepseek model initially flagged the download domain but correctly self-corrected, recognizing it as a vendor-owned domain and not an injection.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed with an HTTP 400 error on the PKGBUILD
openrouter/free failed to parse the model response and is marked as advisory
false_positives: deepseek initially flagged the codeiumdata.com domain as unrelated to devin.ai, but correctly self-corrected upon realizing Codeium is the vendor behind both Devin and Windsurf.
learnings: Models may lack knowledge of corporate ownership structures (e.g., Codeium owning both Devin and Windsurf), leading to false positives regarding download domains. The 'second look' mechanism successfully resolved this.
Ensure robust error handling and retry logic for LLM API calls to prevent inconclusive verdicts due to transient HTTP 400 errors or parse failures.
